page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual machine within the High Performance product line. It is configured with 1 shared vCPU based on the AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 2.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Hardware vector and cryptographic instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In single-threaded execution, the instance demonstrates high instruction throughput, achieving a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3314.98 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 13.91 GB/sec. However, because the instance relies on a single shared execution core, its multi-core stress-ng performance and aggregate PassMark CPU score (2937.11) place it in the lower benchmark quartiles compared to multi-core instances.

Memory and system subsystem metrics reflect typical entry-tier shared resources. Potentially uncached memory bandwidth registers at 35.88 GB/sec for large block reads and 28.69 GB/sec for writes. Web serving throughput reaches 1.63 GB/sec, while in-memory operations measure at 2.52 million Redis SET operations per second. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing on a small 135M parameter model reaches 312.66 tokens/sec, and text generation reaches 109.93 tokens/sec.

This server provides a cost-efficient resource footprint for light single-threaded background tasks, small-scale web serving, utility scripts, microservices, and development environments where single-core bursts and NVMe storage are required without the overhead of dedicated multi-core hardware.
description: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is a budget-tier virtual machine from the High Performance server family, provisioned with 1 shared vCPU from the AMD EPYC x86_64 processor line at 2.0 GHz and 2.0 GB of system memory. Storage is bundled with 50 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside 1 public IPv4 address and no GPU acceleration. The instance incorporates AVX-512, VAES, and SHA instruction set extensions, contributing to strong single-core compute performance, as shown by a top-tier stress-ng single-core result of 3314.98 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 13.91 GB/sec. Multi-core compute and overall memory throughput remain modest due to the single shared core constraint. The configuration is best aligned with lightweight workloads such as microservices, low-traffic web serving, single-threaded processing scripts, and cost-conscious development or testing environments.
